questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of a redox reaction?

options.text: Rusting of iron in the presence of oxygen and moisture

questions.explanation: Rusting involves iron (Fe) being oxidised to $\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$, making it a redox reaction. The other options involve physical changes or simple dissolution without electron transfer.
questions.hint: Look for the reaction where electron transfer occurs.

questions.question_text: In the reaction $\text{Zn} + \text{CuSO}_4 \rightarrow \text{ZnSO}_4 + \text{Cu}$, which substance is oxidised?
questions.explanation: Zinc (Zn) loses electrons and is oxidised to $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ in zinc sulphate. Copper ions ($\text{Cu}^{2+}$) gain electrons and are reduced to Cu metal. This is also a displacement reaction.

questions.question_text: Which of the following reactions requires a diagram showing the movement of electrons?
questions.explanation: Redox reactions involve the transfer of electrons between species. A diagram showing electron movement clearly illustrates oxidation (electron loss) and reduction (electron gain).
questions.diagram_description: A clean scientific diagram showing electron transfer in a redox reaction. Left side: Zn atom losing 2 electrons (labelled 'Oxidation'). Right side: Cu²⁺ ion gaining 2 electrons (labelled 'Reduction'). Arrows showing 2e⁻ moving from Zn to Cu²⁺. White background, 800x500 pixels, clear labels.
